evals.prompt: Here is a job description I want to apply to: https://explore.jobs.netflix.net/careers/job/790313736490?microsite=netflix.com — it's the Data Analyst, Production Finance Operations & Innovation role at Netflix in LA. I've uploaded my resume. Help me tailor it for this role.
evals.expected_output: The skill should: (1) research Netflix culture/values/interview process with credible sources, (2) produce a research brief with confidence-tagged findings, (3) conduct adaptive Q&A rounds drawing out relevant experience from the user, (4) generate specific tailored bullet points using language that mirrors Netflix values and the JD, (5) propose clear REPLACE/ADD/KEEP changes to the existing resume, (6) generate final DOCX and PDF after approval
expectations: Research brief includes Netflix culture values with source citations
Research brief mentions Freedom and Responsibility or keeper test
Q&A questions reference specific job requirements from the JD (SQL, stakeholder management, ad hoc analysis)
Q&A questions are informed by Netflix values, not generic
Bullet points include specific metrics or quantified impact from user's answers
Bullet points use language that mirrors the JD terminology (e.g., production finance, vendor spend, global markets)
Proposed changes use REPLACE/ADD/KEEP format showing old vs new
Skill does not fabricate experience the user did not provide
Skill waits for user approval before generating final documents
Final output includes both DOCX and PDF

evals.prompt: I want to apply to this role: Lumin Digital is hiring a Product Data Analyst (remote, $125K-$145K). It's a Series B fintech startup. The role focuses on product analytics, dashboard development, KPI reporting, and requires 3-5 years with SQL, Tableau, and Python. Preferred: experience with Pendo, Google Analytics, or similar product analytics tools. Fintech/SaaS experience preferred but not required. Here's my resume.
evals.expected_output: The skill should: (1) attempt research on Lumin Digital and be transparent about limited public info, (2) confidence-tag findings appropriately (lower confidence for a startup with less public data), (3) ask the user to fill gaps in company knowledge, (4) still produce useful bullet points despite thin research, (5) recognize the user's strong BI/dashboard background as a close match
expectations: Skill is transparent about limited public information on Lumin Digital's culture
Research findings include confidence tags distinguishing strong evidence from inference
Skill asks the user to fill gaps when research is thin
Q&A questions still reference specific JD requirements (product analytics, KPI reporting, fintech)
Bullet points highlight the user's dashboard and BI experience as directly relevant
Skill does not fabricate company culture details it couldn't verify
Proposed changes recognize existing resume strengths rather than rewriting everything
Skill waits for user approval before generating final documents

evals.prompt: I found this Disney Lead Data Analyst role in New York — it's on the Disney Entertainment & ESPN Product & Technology team, $148K-$199K. Requires a quant degree or equivalent, experience with Python/R, data visualization (Tableau), experimentation, and advanced analytics. I actually worked at Disney before (see my resume). Help me target my resume for this.
evals.expected_output: The skill should: (1) research Disney's current culture and this specific team, (2) recognize the user's prior Disney experience as a major asset, (3) focus Q&A on what's changed since the user worked there and how to position for a senior/lead role, (4) propose refinements rather than a full rewrite, (5) help frame the career arc from Disney contract analyst to returning as a lead
expectations: Skill recognizes the user previously worked at Disney from the resume
Research covers Disney's current culture and the specific ESPN/Product & Technology team
Q&A questions focus on growth since the Disney stint, not basic experience mapping
Q&A explores how to frame the return-to-Disney narrative as a strength
Bullet points for the Disney section are refined/elevated, not completely rewritten
Skill positions the user's career progression (Disney → Nike → Wells Fargo → Pinterest → Apple) as a narrative arc
Proposed changes are targeted refinements, not a wholesale rewrite
Skill waits for user approval before generating final documents
